literal_source_claim_en: Root-space decomposition of a semisimple Lie algebra.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only a root-space decomposition gloss. It omits the coefficient field, characteristic, finite dimension, splitting or algebraic-closure hypotheses, semisimple and Cartan encodings, ordinary versus generalized root spaces, the finite root index, spanning and independence components, whether bracket and bilinear-form companion clauses belong to the root, and all boundary cases. Selecting a standard complex or IsKilling formulation at intake would add or change mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: the selected source must fix the scalar field and universe, algebraic closure or splitting, characteristic, finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra, Cartan data and its encoding, root-index type, ordinary or generalized spaces, and internal-direct-sum representation.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not say whether the root asserts only root-space spanning, an internal direct sum, or the larger package including bracket grading, orthogonality, and opposite-root pairing.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is source-selected; scope-map.md lists the required boundary decisions.
candidate_scope_not_credited: a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field is the internal direct sum of a chosen Cartan subalgebra and its finitely many nonzero ordinary root spaces

the full source package adding bracket compatibility, bilinear-form orthogonality, and nondegenerate opposite-root pairings

zero and top Cartan candidates and the existence-versus-explicit-choice boundary
semisimple direct sums and repeated root dimensions

positive characteristic and fields where ordinary and generalized root spaces differ

excluded_substitutions: real symmetric-pair or Cartan-involution decomposition g = k + p
group-level KAK, polar, or Iwasawa decomposition
spanning by generalized root spaces without the independence/direct-sum component
an IsKilling-only theorem silently replacing the received semisimple theorem

Cartan matrix classification, highest-weight classification, or semisimple Lie algebra classification
a structure or hypothesis storing the desired decomposition
